terms.large-load customer: a covered non-residential computing or data facility with peak demand of at least 100 megawatts at one site or campus
terms.incremental cost: the additional grid-upgrade cost needed to serve that particular large customer

explainBack: The House approved a proposal, but it is not law. If enacted, it would make state regulators and nonregulated utilities consider a standard for allocating a qualifying large computing site’s upgrade costs, while leaving the actual determination and any household-rate effect to later decisions.
unseenTransfer: For another headline saying Congress made an industry pay, separate the chamber vote from enactment, read whether the law requires consideration or adoption, and identify the local regulator or rate case that would create the real charge.
